subject: OBG
title: Normal Labor Stages & Partograph Interpretation
preview: Assess labor through maternal and fetal wellbeing, cervical change and the overall pattern of progress rather than a rigid clock alone.

sections.title: Observe progress in context
points: Document cervical findings, contractions, descent and maternal/fetal condition with an appropriate care tool.
Active labor and the pace of change vary substantially between individuals.

sections.title: When progress appears slow
points: Review maternal and fetal status and consider presentation, position, contractions and support before selecting intervention.
Escalation decisions are based on a combination of findings and established maternity protocols.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: A single slow cervical examination is not proof of obstructed labor.
Do not apply an outdated universal dilation threshold without context.

quickRevision: Normal labor has variable progress; a single hourly cervical-dilation rule should not replace clinical assessment.
Evaluate contraction quality, fetal presentation, maternal physiology and fetal heart rate patterns.
The WHO Labour Care Guide promotes individualized, evidence-based intrapartum monitoring.

quiz.question: What is assessed using a labor progress chart?
options: Cervical dilation and labor progress over time
quiz.explanation: Cervical dilation and labor progress over time. Stages of Labor: • First Stage: From onset of true labor pains to full cervical dilatation (10 cm).
